title: Non-Verbal Reasoning: Mirror, Water & Paper Folding
shortDescription: Mirror flips left-right, water flips up-down, paper folding punches through every layer — three different transformations, easy to tell apart once you name them.
genZNote: Mirror image, water image, paper folding — three different party tricks, three different rules. Name which trick you're looking at before you pick an option.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.body: Each of these three question types applies a SPECIFIC, different geometric transformation to a figure. Misidentifying which transformation is being asked for is the main source of wrong answers — the fastest fix is naming the transformation before scanning the options.

sections.heading: Mirror Image
sections.body: A mirror image reflects the figure LEFT-TO-RIGHT across a vertical line (as if a mirror were held vertically along one edge of the figure) — like reading the figure in a mirror placed to its side. Numbers and letters typically appear reversed left-to-right; positions of elements swap left and right, but top and bottom stay the same.

sections.heading: Water Image
sections.body: A water image reflects the figure TOP-TO-BOTTOM across a horizontal line — as if the figure were reflected in still water below it. Top and bottom swap; left and right stay the same. This is the transformation most often confused with mirror image, since both are 'reflections' but across perpendicular axes.

sections.heading: Paper Folding & Punching
sections.body: A paper-folding question shows a sheet folded one or more times, then punched with a hole (or a shape cut out), and asks what the sheet looks like unfolded. The technique: work BACKWARDS from the last fold to the first, mirroring the punched hole's position across each fold line in reverse order — every fold line the hole crosses adds a mirrored hole on the other side of that line once unfolded.

steps.name: Identify the fold sequence
steps.explanation: A square sheet is folded in half vertically, then in half horizontally, then punched with one hole near a corner of the small folded square.
steps.purpose: Note both fold lines and their order — you'll undo them in reverse.

steps.name: Unfold in reverse order
steps.explanation: Undo the horizontal fold first: the single hole becomes two holes, mirrored across the horizontal fold line. Then undo the vertical fold: each of those two holes becomes two more, mirrored across the vertical fold line — four holes total.
steps.purpose: Each fold you undo doubles the hole count via a mirror reflection across that specific fold line.

sections.heading: Common Traps
bullets: Confusing mirror image (left-right flip) with water image (top-bottom flip) — always check which axis the question specifies or implies.
Undoing paper folds in the same order they were made instead of in REVERSE order.
Forgetting that a fold line the hole does NOT cross doesn't add a mirrored hole across that particular line.

sections.heading: Exam Strategy
bullets: Name the transformation type out loud/in your head ('this is a water image — top-bottom flip') before looking at the answer options.

For paper folding, count the number of folds; the final unfolded hole count is often (but not always, depending on hole position relative to fold lines) a power of 2 related to the fold count — use this as a quick sanity check on your answer.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Mirror image flips left-right, water image flips top-bottom, and paper folding requires undoing folds in reverse order, mirroring the punched hole across each fold line.
keyFacts: Mirror image: reflects left-right, top/bottom unchanged.
Water image: reflects top-bottom, left/right unchanged.
Paper folding: unfold in REVERSE order of folding, mirroring the hole across each fold line as you go.
commonConfusion: Mirror and water images are both 'reflections' but across perpendicular axes — one flips left-right, the other flips top-bottom.

highYieldFacts: Paper folding is always undone in reverse order of how the folds were made.
commonTraps: Mixing up which axis mirror image vs water image reflects across.
mustRemember: Name the transformation type before scanning the answer options.
